title: Effective-resistance average bound for intrinsic kinetic rows
question: Can the intrinsic kinetic graph use an electrical effective-resistance average to produce a tree-independent finite Poincare lower bound and a cleaner target for cutoff/volume uniformity?

new_perspective.principle: Use the Green kernel of the conductance Laplacian rather than a selected path family. Pairwise effective resistance controls every potential difference by the graph energy, and the Gibbs pair average gives one explicit global variance constant.
route: For each conditional law pi, form the symmetric momentum conductance c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi) and its connected Laplacian L.
Compute the Moore--Penrose inverse L^+ on the constant-orthogonal subspace and the effective resistances R_xy=(e_x-e_y)^T L^+(e_x-e_y).
Set Rbar_pi=sum_{x<y} pi_x*pi_y*R_xy. Pairwise Cauchy--Schwarz gives Var_pi(f)<=Rbar_pi E(f), hence Rbar_pi^(-1) is a finite lower bound independent of tree choice.

Repeat the full R-404 actual-likelihood grid, compare the resistance bound with the exact intrinsic gap and the R-407 maximum-tree bound, and record the smallest positive Laplacian eigenvalue and largest resistance as conditioning inputs.
Use a diagonal-q disconnected mutation and a three-node factor-of-two toy graph in the hostile lane; a line/tree choice is no longer part of the theorem.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A promoted route would require a cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform bound on the weighted Green kernel or its pair-average, plus a common-core identification with the Hamiltonian shell. This replaces arbitrary path geometry by an electrical/heat-kernel estimate but remains a finite interface here.

finite_theorem.tree_independence: The finite certificate depends only on L^+; no spanning tree or path choice enters the bound
finite_theorem.normalization: The pair sum is over unordered x<y, so no extra factor 2 enters the bound

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar nonnegativity and finite pair-sum bookkeeping; pseudoinverses, graph spectra, Gibbs rows and all uniform/QFT limits remain in the executable/open boundary.

promotion_criteria: Prove a cutoff-independent weighted Green-kernel or effective-resistance-average upper bound on one Hamiltonian common core.
Control source, phase, volume, orientation and exhaustion dependence and the connectedness/conditioning of the intrinsic graph.
Transfer the resistance lower bound to the R-399 shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur coarse/residual decomposition before any common-alpha or GNS promotion.
stop_conditions: If the resistance average diverges or the positive Laplacian spectrum collapses under a validated cutoff/volume stress, retain this as a finite diagnostic and do not replace the shell proof.
If the graph is disconnected, the pseudoinverse zero mode is mishandled, or the finite path residual becomes negative, stop and record the exact obstruction.
Finite resistance positivity is not a uniform, phase-selection, common-core, GNS, physical-gap or QFT theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite effective-resistance checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The electrical certificate removes tree choice from the finite bound and exposes a Green-kernel uniformity target; it does not establish that target in a regulator or thermodynamic limit.
